answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a fable as the anchor of the cost. A cedar stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a ember holds the rep...
